datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Phoenix Thermal and Electrical Conductivity Probe (TECP) relative humidity sensor in situ measurements (raw DNRH and board temperature Tb; recalibrated frost point Tf, water vapor pressure e, and RH)
datasets.instrument_sensor: Thermal and Electrical Conductivity Probe (TECP) relative humidity (RH) sensor
datasets.measurement_observable: Atmospheric relative humidity (with respect to ice), frost point temperature (Tf), water vapor pressure (e), raw RH output (DNRH), sensor/electronics board temperature (Tb)
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ time-series environmental sensor measurements
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: PHX sol 1 (Ls ~77°) to sol 150 (Ls ~148°); typical sampling rate 1.2 s during ~30 min blocks a few times per sol; extended blocks ~30 min to ~20 hr; in-soil campaign sols 46–47, 54–55, 69–71, 86, 98, 103–104, 111, 119, 122–124, 149–150; examples cited: sol 54 around noon (max e ~1.4 Pa), sol 122 ~2 a.m. (min e ~0.005 Pa); day/night comparison windows used include 10:30–13:50 LTST and 00:00–04:00 LTST
datasets.location_coverage: Phoenix landing site (68.2°N, 234.2°E); measurements in air at heights 0 to ~2.2 m depending on robotic arm position; some analyses note measurements 3 cm above ground and a period at 0.8 m height (sols 55–56, 6–8 a.m.)
datasets.how_used: Primary dataset analyzed. Authors apply a new lab-derived recalibration (translation function and calibration function) to TECP raw DNRH and Tb flight measurements to compute updated Tf, e, and RH; then evaluate diurnal/seasonal variability, day/night ratios, and implications for regolith-atmosphere H2O exchange and brine formation potential.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Phoenix Meteorological Station (MET) air temperature measurements at 2 m height
datasets.measurement_observable: Air temperature (used to compute RH at 2 m when combined with TECP-derived water vapor pressure)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: During the Phoenix mission (context indicates sols 1–150; specific times not stated)
datasets.location_coverage: Phoenix landing site (68.2°N, 234.2°E); temperature at 2 m above ground
datasets.how_used: Used as an independent temperature reference (colder than TECP board temperature due to TECP electronics heating) to convert TECP-derived water vapor pressure to RH at 2 m height (assuming constant near-surface water vapor pressure vertically); used in discussion of saturation/frost/fog conditions and in brine-stability comparison.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) relative humidity data (used in Figures 9 and 10)
datasets.measurement_observable: Near-surface relative humidity (and associated temperature context for brine-stability comparison)
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ time-series environmental sensor measurements
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Nighttime REMS values used for day/night ratios: ~04:00–06:00 (LTST not specified for MSL in paper); broader time span not stated (paper notes REMS operating >2,400 sols as of May 2019, but specific subset used here not further specified)
datasets.location_coverage: MSL landing site at Gale crater (4.5°S, 37.4°E); used at/near ground and at 1.6 m height (as plotted in brine stability diagram)
datasets.how_used: Used for comparison to Phoenix: (1) day/night water vapor pressure ratio comparison (nighttime REMS values paired with daytime ChemCam-derived values) and (2) RH–temperature points for assessing deliquescence/brine stability at the MSL site (Figure 10).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) ChemCam passive sky spectroscopy-derived water vapor pressure around noon (as plotted in Figures 8–10)
datasets.measurement_observable: Daytime water vapor pressure derived from water vapor column abundance retrievals (passive sky spectroscopy)
datasets.data_type_product_type: Derived time series / retrieved atmospheric quantity (water vapor)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Around noon (daytime) at the MSL site; additional timing for ratios referenced as "~noon" (no dates/sol ranges specified)
datasets.location_coverage: MSL landing site at Gale crater (4.5°S, 37.4°E)
datasets.how_used: Used as an independent daytime estimate of water vapor pressure at Gale crater for comparison with Phoenix seasonal/diurnal maxima (Figure 8) and to compute MSL day/night water vapor pressure ratios (paired with REMS nighttime values) and for brine-stability comparison (Figure 10).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Phoenix Surface Stereo Imager (SSI) precipitable water vapor column abundance (PWC) retrievals at the Phoenix landing site (used for comparison/constraints)
datasets.measurement_observable: Retrieved precipitable water vapor column abundance (PWC); used to estimate/compare near-surface daytime water vapor pressure (e) bounds
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Daytime SSI retrievals referenced as between 13:00 and 17:00 LMST; within Phoenix mission season (solar longitude coverage shown in comparisons; exact sols/dates not specified)
datasets.how_used: Used as an independent dataset to (a) justify/choose conservative upper bounds for daytime near-surface water vapor pressure used in calibration sensitivity studies and (b) compare Phoenix TECP-derived maximum diurnal water vapor pressure against contemporaneous SSI-derived values (Figure 8).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM) precipitable water vapor column abundance retrievals at the Phoenix landing site (used for comparison/constraints)
datasets.instrument_sensor: Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM)
datasets.measurement_observable: Retrieved atmospheric water vapor column abundance / equivalent water vapor pressure estimates at Phoenix location
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Referenced CRISM measurements at ~14:00 LMST at the Phoenix location; within Phoenix mission season (exact sols/dates not specified)
datasets.how_used: Used as an independent orbital dataset to support/limit assumed daytime upper bounds of water vapor pressure for warm/dry conditions in the TECP recalibration and to compare seasonal evolution of maximum diurnal water vapor pressure at Phoenix (Figure 8).

query_generation_agent_results.output_text: {"paper_title":"Relative Humidity on Mars: New Results From the Phoenix TECP Sensor","queries":[{"query":"I need the Phoenix lander TECP atmospheric humidity sensor time series over the full surface mission (about sols 1–150) at the high northern latitude landing site, including the raw humidity channel output and electronics board temperature plus the recalibrated frost point, water vapor pressure, and relative humidity (with respect to ice), to quantify daytime minima versus nighttime near-saturation behavior and diurnal variability.","data_identifier":"urn:nasa:pds:phx_meca:data_tecp_rhs","data_identifier_type":"collection_lid"},{"query":"To correctly interpret TECP humidity observations taken at variable heights (near-surface up to a couple meters) and during intervals when the probe was inserted into the regolith, I need the Phoenix lander robotic arm derived/engineering products that allow reconstruction of arm configuration versus time so I can map each TECP humidity sample to its measurement geometry and separate in-air from in-soil acquisition periods.","data_identifier":"urn:nasa:pds:phx_ra::1.1","data_identifier_type":"lidvid"}]}

output_parsed.paper_title: Relative Humidity on Mars: New Results From the Phoenix TECP Sensor

queries.query: I need the Phoenix lander TECP atmospheric humidity sensor time series over the full surface mission (about sols 1–150) at the high northern latitude landing site, including the raw humidity channel output and electronics board temperature plus the recalibrated frost point, water vapor pressure, and relative humidity (with respect to ice), to quantify daytime minima versus nighttime near-saturation behavior and diurnal variability.

To correctly interpret TECP humidity observations taken at variable heights (near-surface up to a couple meters) and during intervals when the probe was inserted into the regolith, I need the Phoenix lander robotic arm derived/engineering products that allow reconstruction of arm configuration versus time so I can map each TECP humidity sample to its measurement geometry and separate in-air from in-soil acquisition periods.

queries.query: Need raw in situ Phoenix lander Meteorological Station pressure and air-temperature time series (seconds-scale cadence) acquired during the Mars surface mission to characterize boundary-layer temperature variability and to compute near-surface relative humidity when combined with TECP-derived water vapor pressure.

Assemble the Phoenix lander Meteorological Station archive of air-temperature measurements at approximately meter-scale height above the surface to provide an independent temperature reference for converting TECP water vapor pressure into relative humidity and for evaluating nighttime saturation/frost conditions at the Phoenix landing site on Mars.

queries.query: Use Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM atmospheric retrieval products to characterize column-integrated water vapor variability over Mars, with emphasis on the northern polar plains during the Phoenix surface mission season for comparison against in situ humidity constraints.

Using Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM derived atmospheric retrievals, isolate precipitable water vapor (or equivalent vapor pressure) estimates for the Phoenix landing site region acquired at mid-afternoon local time to provide an independent orbital constraint on near-surface humidity under warm, dry conditions.

final_output.query: I need the Phoenix lander TECP atmospheric humidity sensor time series over the full surface mission (about sols 1–150) at the high northern latitude landing site, including the raw humidity channel output and electronics board temperature plus the recalibrated frost point, water vapor pressure, and relative humidity (with respect to ice), to quantify daytime minima versus nighttime near-saturation behavior and diurnal variability.

To correctly interpret TECP humidity observations taken at variable heights (near-surface up to a couple meters) and during intervals when the probe was inserted into the regolith, I need the Phoenix lander robotic arm derived/engineering products that allow reconstruction of arm configuration versus time so I can map each TECP humidity sample to its measurement geometry and separate in-air from in-soil acquisition periods.

Need raw in situ Phoenix lander Meteorological Station pressure and air-temperature time series (seconds-scale cadence) acquired during the Mars surface mission to characterize boundary-layer temperature variability and to compute near-surface relative humidity when combined with TECP-derived water vapor pressure.

Assemble the Phoenix lander Meteorological Station archive of air-temperature measurements at approximately meter-scale height above the surface to provide an independent temperature reference for converting TECP water vapor pressure into relative humidity and for evaluating nighttime saturation/frost conditions at the Phoenix landing site on Mars.

Calibrated near-surface relative humidity with the associated air/ground temperature context from the Curiosity rover meteorology package in Gale crater, using the fully processed REMS environmental time-series appropriate for diurnal water-vapor variability and brine-stability assessment.

Raw, unprocessed REMS humidity-channel and supporting housekeeping/engineering measurements from the Curiosity rover in Gale crater, intended for rebuilding the calibration pipeline from instrument units to physical relative humidity (including nighttime/pre-dawn comparisons).

Characterize peak daytime (local-noon) near-surface water vapor pressure at Gale crater using Curiosity ChemCam derived atmospheric retrieval products, to constrain diurnal maxima relevant to surface–atmosphere H2O exchange and brine-stability analyses.

Assemble Curiosity ChemCam raw passive sky spectroscopy observations acquired near local noon over the mission timeline at Gale crater, and use them to independently retrieve water vapor column abundance and convert to water vapor pressure for cross-instrument humidity comparisons.

For the Phoenix lander at the Mars polar landing site, I need the Surface Stereo Imager derived atmospheric products used to retrieve precipitable water vapor column abundance from daytime observations (midafternoon local solar times) across the full landed mission season, to place bounds on near-surface water vapor pressure under the warmest/driest conditions.

Compile the full Phoenix lander Surface Stereo Imager atmospheric dataset (including derived products plus supporting context/documentation) spanning the entire 2008 surface mission interval on Mars, to evaluate seasonal behavior of atmospheric column properties such as aerosol opacity and water vapor constraints over the Phoenix landing site region.

Use Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM atmospheric retrieval products to characterize column-integrated water vapor variability over Mars, with emphasis on the northern polar plains during the Phoenix surface mission season for comparison against in situ humidity constraints.

Using Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CRISM derived atmospheric retrievals, isolate precipitable water vapor (or equivalent vapor pressure) estimates for the Phoenix landing site region acquired at mid-afternoon local time to provide an independent orbital constraint on near-surface humidity under warm, dry conditions.
